title: MZ How to get status window to appear more than 4 party members

posts.author: Darkmoon9
posts.body:
Hi, I am currenty using Visustella Sideways Battle UI in conjunction wih Darkneondragontwins Party Plugin. I have managed to get it to work pretty well. Only remaining issue is that the Status UI does not appear for temporary party members added with summon skillif the party exceeds 4 actors with the summon. Is there a way to add Status UI with 5th and subsequent members of the party?
Edit. Added image to demonstrate what I mean. Notice how the summoned imp does not have a health bar or mana bar displayed. I tried other ui methods and they all work, escept the Visustella sideways battle ui, which is the one I want to use. Another image was provided showing the status screens being added properly with the default layout.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
I quickly checked the plugin and it targets the battle status window (since that's used in base game). That VS sideview battle UI creates a number of windows based on your max battle members at battle start I think. So if you change your max battle members mid battle, like that plugin seems to do, there won't be a window to show new stuff.
So you can try to make a new window there when you summon the dude and remove it when they leave. Or just try to make an additional window at battle start which is probably easier, but you still probably have to find a way to hide the stuff when the summon leaves.
But yeah if you write to console that
SceneManager._scene.createSideviewUiBattleStatusWindows
and click the function, even though it's obfuscated you can see that it seems to check max battle members in the loop. Just copy paste that and make a plugin where you add +1 to the formula so that it creates the fifth window there.

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body: You need to change the max party size outside from battles. There's no standard way in RPG Maker to do that inside, so programming a plugin to support that isn't trivial. Therefore, most devs don't implement it at all instead of implementing something that is risky to break.

posts.author: rpgLord69
Aerosys
posts.body: This is what I meant with "there's no standard". Windows are initialized on battle start, then the plugins usually don't support adding or removing a window/column/row dynamically.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
Cool.
For your new question, I didn't check the plugin code, but if you don't change the number of normal characters mid battle, I guess one way of doing it is using VS pre-battle common event to store the number of
$gameParty.allBattleMembers().length
to a variable. Then you can use VS JS Skill Enable notetags for the summon skills to check that (change variable id and amount of summons to what you want):
<JS Skill Enable>
enabled = $gameParty.allBattleMembers().length < $gameVariables.value(100) + 2;
</JS Skill Enable>

I did manage to figure out a solution, I simply made all summon skills share a cooldown of 99 turns, which resets at the start of each battle. Which effectively made it so that a single summoner can only summon one minion per battle, to a maximum of 4 minions if all 4 actors are classes that can summon, for a total of 8 party members. Noticed the summon plugin had no upper limit, so without it, you could summon a ridiculous number of additional actors, more than a bit broken.
Even with the global cooldown, summoner classes like the warlock or ranger are probably pretty strong. Might even be broken.
